draft.title: Media and sport
card: The media includes television, radio, newspapers, websites and social media. It decides which sports get coverage, and coverage helps decide which sports people know and follow.
Sports with a lot of coverage tend to gain fans, players and sponsors. Sports with little coverage can stay small, even when many people play them.
The media can shape how athletes are seen. What it chooses to show and say, such as skill, looks or personal life, affects the image the public has of them.
Media coverage can bring in money. Broadcasters pay for the right to show games, and sponsors pay to be seen by large audiences. This money helps fund sport.
draft.remember: Coverage shapes what people watch, how athletes are seen and where sport's money comes from.

a.q: Why does a sport with regular television coverage often find it easier to raise money?
opts: Sponsors pay to reach the large audience it attracts
Television channels run the sport's clubs and teams
Coverage means more people play the sport for free
Broadcasters decide the rules so the sport is fairer
a.why: Regular coverage gives a sport a large audience. Sponsors and broadcasters pay to reach that audience, which brings money in. Coverage does not mean the media runs the clubs, as the media only shows the sport.
a.clue: Think about who pays to be seen by a big audience.

b.q: A netball league in regional Victoria has many players but almost no coverage. Its games are not shown on TV or online. What is the most likely effect?
opts: It may struggle to attract sponsors and new fans
It will lose most of its current players straight away
It will earn more from broadcasters than popular sports
It will become more popular because it is less known
b.why: With little coverage, few people outside the league see it, so sponsors have less reason to pay. Many people can still play, so players will not necessarily leave at once. The media shapes popularity and funding, not whether people take part.
b.clue: Sponsors pay to be seen by an audience.

a.best: Sponsors pay to reach the large audience it attracts

b.best: It may struggle to attract sponsors and new fans

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'), while every distractor says 'will'. A student can pick it without knowing the idea.

Why (b) says the media shapes popularity and funding 'not whether people take part'. The card says sports with a lot of coverage tend to gain 'fans, players and sponsors', so coverage does affect participation.

Why (a) says 'the media only shows the sport'. The card says the media decides coverage and shapes how sports and athletes are seen, so 'only' overstates the point. Some media companies have also owned teams.
The clue 'who pays to be seen by a big audience' almost restates the right option ('Sponsors pay to reach the large audience'), so it gives the answer away.

a.q: Why does a sport with regular television coverage often find it easier to raise money?
opts: Sponsors pay to reach the large audience it attracts
Coverage cuts the cost of running games and venues
Governments must fund every sport shown on television
Broadcasters set the rules, so the sport costs less to run
a.why: Regular coverage gives a sport a large audience. Sponsors and broadcasters pay to reach that audience, which brings money in. Coverage does not lower the cost of running games or venues: it brings in money rather than cutting what the sport spends.
a.clue: Who gains when many people are watching?

b.q: A netball league in regional Victoria has many players but almost no coverage. Its games are not shown on TV or online. What is the most likely effect?
opts: It struggles to attract sponsors and new fans
It loses most of its current players straight away
It earns more from broadcasters than popular sports do
It grows more popular because it is less well known
b.why: With little coverage, few people outside the league see it, so sponsors have less reason to pay and fewer new fans find it. Losing most players at once is tempting, but sports with little coverage can still have many people playing them, so a sudden loss of current players is not the likely effect.
b.clue: Think about who would notice a league that no one can watch.
